title: Annotatio VI §.III (2): Augustine/Jerome/Origen — impious do not eat the vivifying flesh
pass_a_gloss: (2) Concerning all the remaining who communicate unworthily, for this sole cause that they are not in communion with Christ by faith but in communion of demons because of impiety, Augustine’s judgment is abundantly known — not only his — when in City of God 21.25 he says: It is not to be said that he eats Christ’s body who is not in Christ’s body. And a little later: Nor are those to be said to eat Christ’s body who are not to be counted in Christ’s members: For they cannot at once be members of Christ and of a Harlot. And again likewise Tract. 26 on John; and also St. JEROME on Isaiah 66: Those who are not Holy in Body and Spirit neither eat Christ’s flesh nor drink his blood, of whom it is said: Who eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life. And of a still somewhat older Writer, ORIGEN, Comm. on Matt. 15: Christ, he says, is true food; whoever eats him will live forever, of which no impious person can eat. For if it were possible that anyone persisting in impiety eat the Word made flesh, it would never have been written: Whoever eats this bread will live forever.
pass_b_english: (2) For all other unworthy communicants — not in Christ by faith but in demon-communion by impiety — Augustine (Civ. Dei 21.25): one not in Christ’s body does not eat Christ’s body; members of Christ and of a harlot cannot be the same (also Tract. Joh. 26).

Jerome (Isa. 66): the unholy in body and spirit neither eat the flesh nor drink the blood that gives eternal life. Origen (Matt. 15): Christ is true food no impious can eat — else “whoever eats this bread lives forever” would be false.
source_text: (2) De reliquis indignè communicantibus omnibus, eam solam ob causam, quòd in communione cum Christo haud sunt per fidem, sed in communione dæmoniorum ob impietatem, notum abunde est, non AUGUSTINI tantum judicium, quando Lib. 21. de Civitate DEI Cap. 25. Non dicendum, inquit, eum manducare corpus Christi, qui in corpore non est Christi. Et paulò post: Nec isti dicendi sunt manducare corpus Christi, qui nec in membris sunt computandi Christi: Non enim possunt simul esse membra Christi, & Meretricis. Et rursus, simile quid Tract. 26. in Joh.; Sed & S. HIERONYMI in cap. 66. Esaiæ: Qui non Sancti sunt, & Corpore & Spiritu, nec carnem Christi edunt, nec sanguinem ejus bibunt, de quibus dictum: Qui manducat carnem meam & bibit sanguinem meum, habet vitam æternam. Et adhuc paulò antiquioris Scriptoris, ORIGINIS nempe, Comm. in Matth. cap. 15. Christus, inquit, verus cibus est, quicunque illum edit, vivet in æternum, de quo impius nullus edere potest. Nam si possibile esset quemquam in impietate persistentem, verbum caro factum edere, nunquam scriptum foret: Quicunque edit hunc panem, vivet in æternum.
